title: Heritage sites in Madhya Pradesh: Khajuraho, Sanchi, Bhimbetka
seo_title: Heritage Sites in Madhya Pradesh: Historical Places
meta_description: Heritage sites in Madhya Pradesh: UNESCO Khajuraho, Sanchi and Bhimbetka, plus Mandu, Gwalior, Orchha, Udayagiri, Bhojpur, Ujjain and Maheshwar, with tips.
summary: Madhya Pradesh has three UNESCO World Heritage Sites: the Khajuraho temples (1986), the Buddhist monuments at Sanchi (1989) and the Bhimbetka rock shelters (2003). It also holds Mandu, Gwalior Fort, Orchha, the Udayagiri caves, Bhojpur, Ujjain, Omkareshwar and Maheshwar, making it one of the richest states for Indian history.

sections.h2: Why Madhya Pradesh is the heart of Indian archaeology
paras: Central India sits between north and south, and almost every period of Indian history has left a mark here. Bhimbetka's painted shelters show people living in the Vindhyan hills for many thousands of years. The Mauryans and Shungas built and enlarged the Sanchi stupas, the Guptas cut the Udayagiri caves, the Paramaras and Chandelas built great temples, and the sultans of Malwa, the Mughals, the Bundela rajas, the Scindias and the Holkars followed.

For a teacher, that means a single state can carry a whole syllabus. Our multi-day [Central India: rock art and Buddhist archaeology](central-india-rock-art-and-buddhist-archaeology.html) tour and the [Stupas, caves and temples of central India](stupas-caves-and-temples-of-central-india.html) programme are built on exactly this.

sections.h2: UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Madhya Pradesh
paras: Khajuraho (1986) has some 20 surviving temples of the Chandela dynasty, mostly built between about 950 and 1050, out of a much larger number. The Kandariya Mahadeva, Lakshmana and Vishvanatha temples show the Nagara tower at its most complex, and their wall sculpture covers deities, celestial women, daily life and a small share of erotic scenes. Our [Khajuraho architecture deep dive](khajuraho-architecture-deep-dive.html) explains how to read them.

Sanchi (1989) has the Great Stupa, first built in brick under Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE and later enlarged in stone, with four carved gateways (toranas) of about the 1st century BCE to 1st century CE that tell Jataka stories and scenes from the Buddha's life. Our [Sanchi programme](sanchi-stupas-gateways-and-buddhist-art.html) reads each gateway in turn.

Bhimbetka (2003), near Bhopal, has hundreds of rock shelters, many with paintings of animals, hunting, dancing and riders, spanning a very long period from the Mesolithic to historical times. See our [Bhimbetka programme](bhimbetka-painted-shelters-and-prehistoric-landscapes.html) and the guide to [rock art in India](rock-art-in-india.html).

sections.h2: Ancient temples and caves in Madhya Pradesh
paras: The Udayagiri caves near Vidisha were cut around the early 5th century under Chandragupta II, and include the large relief of Varaha, the boar avatar of Vishnu, rescuing the earth. Nearby Vidisha has the Heliodorus pillar of the 2nd century BCE, set up by a Greek envoy who called himself a devotee of Vasudeva. The Bhojeshwar temple at Bhojpur, begun under the Paramara king Bhoja in the 11th century, was never finished; plans for it are engraved on the surrounding rocks.

Other early temples include the Gupta-period temple at Tigawa, the Bateshwar group near Morena (a large cluster of small temples rebuilt from collapse in recent decades), the Chausath Yogini temple at Mitaoli and the temples of Amarkantak. Ujjain, Omkareshwar and Maheshwar are living pilgrimage towns on the Shipra and Narmada.

sections.h2: Prehistory and early history of central India
paras: Madhya Pradesh has one of the longest prehistoric records in India. Acheulean hand axes are common in the Narmada valley, and at Hathnora, near Hoshangabad (Narmadapuram), a fossil skull cap was found in 1982 that is often discussed as among the oldest human fossils from South Asia, though its age and classification are debated. The Son valley and the Vindhyan hills hold many stone tool sites, and Bhimbetka's shelters were occupied long before they were painted.

Farming villages of the Chalcolithic period, such as Navdatoli on the Narmada and Kayatha near Ujjain, show settled life with painted pottery in the 2nd millennium BCE. In the early historic period, Ujjain and Vidisha grew into major cities on the trade route between the Ganga valley and the western coast. Inscriptions at Sanchi record gifts by people from Vidisha, including a guild of ivory carvers who worked on one of the gateways.

This depth is why central India is so good for teaching chronology. In a few days a group can handle stone tools in a museum, see painted shelters, walk a Mauryan and Shunga stupa and stand in a Gupta cave, putting abstract periods into real places.

Gwalior Fort sits on a long sandstone hill and holds the Man Singh palace (late 15th century) with blue tile work, the Teli ka Mandir, the Sas-Bahu temples and large rock-cut Jain figures of the 15th century. A zero in a 9th-century inscription in a small temple here is among the earliest known in India. See our [heritage walk in Gwalior](heritage-walk-in-gwalior.html) guide.

Mandu, the capital of the Malwa sultans, has the Jahaz Mahal, Hindola Mahal, Hoshang Shah's marble tomb and many water systems; see our [Mandu programme](mandu-fortified-plateau-and-water-architecture.html). Orchha, the Bundela capital on the Betwa, has the Jahangir Mahal and Raja Mahal with murals, and riverside chhatris. Bhopal has the Taj-ul-Masajid and the begums' city. Raisen and Chanderi have hill forts.

sections.h2: Planning a heritage trip in Madhya Pradesh
paras: Bhopal is the best base for Sanchi, Vidisha, Udayagiri, Bhimbetka, Bhojpur and Raisen. Gwalior covers Bateshwar and Mitaoli, and Orchha and Khajuraho can follow by road. Indore covers Mandu, Maheshwar, Omkareshwar and Ujjain. October to March is best. Check the ASI website before you go.

faq.q: How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites are there in Madhya Pradesh?
faq.a: Three: the Khajuraho Group of Monuments (1986), the Buddhist Monuments at Sanchi (1989) and the Rock Shelters of Bhimbetka (2003). Gwalior Fort, Mandu and Orchha are on the tentative list but not inscribed.

faq.q: Which historical places in Madhya Pradesh are near Bhopal?
faq.a: Sanchi, Vidisha, the Udayagiri caves, Bhimbetka, Bhojpur and Raisen fort are all within a day trip of Bhopal, and the city itself has the Taj-ul-Masajid, old markets and the State and Tribal museums.

faq.q: How old are the Bhimbetka paintings?
faq.a: They span a very long period. The oldest are usually attributed to the Mesolithic, and the latest are from historical times, with riders and soldiers. Exact dates for individual paintings are often uncertain.

faq.q: Does Talaash Heritage run tours in Madhya Pradesh?
faq.a: Yes. We run day programmes at Sanchi, Bhimbetka, Udayagiri, Bhojpur, Raisen, Mandu and in Bhopal, a two-day Sanchi and Vidisha immersion and a multi-day central India tour, all on request.

posts.hook: An 11th-century architect left his drawings on the rocks.
posts.caption: Around the unfinished Bhojeshwar temple at Bhojpur, plans and profiles are engraved into the stone. They show how the temple was meant to look.

posts.hook: At Sanchi, read the gateways clockwise.
posts.caption: Start at the south gateway and move clockwise. Look for the Buddha shown by symbols, a tree, a wheel, footprints, not as a human figure.
